# ASSP-NG configuration reference

<!-- Generated by 'assp-ng config doc' from the settings registry. Do not edit. -->

Settings live in layered TOML files in `/etc/assp-ng`. Each setting has a level that says where it is allowed:

- `system`: only in `assp-ng.toml`.
- `recipient`: in `default.toml`, `domain.d/<domain>.toml` and `user.d/<address>.toml`; resolved by the recipient address (mailbox, then domain, then default, then built-in).
- `sender`: the same files, resolved by the authenticated user name.

Durations are whole numbers with an optional suffix `s`, `m`, `h` or `d` (for example `90`, `30s`, `15m`, `24h`, `7d`); a bare number means seconds. Unknown keys and keys at a level where they are not allowed are errors.

Besides these values, `assp-ng.toml` holds the `[[listener]]` and `[[tls.certificate]]` tables. A listener has `name`, `kind` (`smtp`, `submission` or `submissions`), `port`, `backend` (`host:port`) and optionally `ipv4`, `ipv6`, `bind4`, `bind6`, `xclient` and `auth`. A listener with `auth = true` needs a loopback backend host, because the credentials reach the backend in plain text. A certificate has `name`, `hostnames`, `cert` and `key`.

| Key | Type | Default | Level | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `instance` | str | `""` | system | Name of this ASSP-NG instance, used in logs and alerts. |
| `hostname` | str | `""` | system | Host name announced in the SMTP banner and headers; empty means the system FQDN. |
| `banner.text` | str | `""` | system | Extra text appended to the SMTP greeting banner. |
| `database.url` | str | `""` | system | Database connection URL for persistent data. |
| `redis.url` | str | `"redis://localhost:6379/0"` | system | Redis connection URL for shared state. |
| `redis.key_prefix` | str | `"asspng:"` | system | Prefix for every key ASSP-NG stores in Redis. |
| `redis.op_timeout_ms` | int | `200` | system | Maximum time in milliseconds for one Redis operation. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `state.on_redis_failure` | str | `"degraded"` | system | Behaviour when Redis fails: degraded keeps working on local memory, tempfail answers with a temporary SMTP error. Allowed: one of degraded, tempfail. |
| `state.failures_to_degrade` | int | `3` | system | Consecutive Redis failures after which the state backend switches to degraded mode. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `state.unreachable_to_degrade_s` | int | `2` | system | Seconds Redis may stay unreachable before the state backend switches to degraded mode; 0 switches at the first failure. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `state.probe_interval_s` | int | `10` | system | Seconds between probes that check whether Redis has recovered. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `state.memory_max_entries` | int | `200000` | system | Maximum number of entries kept in the local in-memory state fallback. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `network.ipv4_prefix` | int | `32` | system | IPv4 prefix length that groups client addresses into one "network" for limits and the penalty box; 32 treats every address on its own, 0 puts all of them in one. Allowed: 0 to 32. |
| `network.ipv6_prefix` | int | `64` | system | IPv6 prefix length that groups client addresses into one "network" for limits and the penalty box; 128 treats every address on its own, 0 puts all of them in one. Allowed: 0 to 128. |
| `limits.net.concurrent` | int | `5` | system | Maximum simultaneous connections from one client network (the addresses grouped by network.ipv4_prefix and network.ipv6_prefix). Allowed: at least 1. |
| `limits.net.connections_per_minute` | int | `30` | system | Maximum new connections per minute from one client network (grouped by network.ipv4_prefix and network.ipv6_prefix). Allowed: at least 1. |
| `limits.instance.concurrent` | int | `500` | system | Maximum simultaneous connections accepted by this instance. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `limits.session.messages` | int | `50` | system | Maximum messages accepted in one SMTP session. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `limits.session.protocol_errors` | int | `5` | system | Protocol errors tolerated in one SMTP session before it is closed. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `limits.session.invalid_recipients` | int | `5` | system | Invalid recipients tolerated in one SMTP session before it is closed. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `limits.message.recipients` | int | `100` | system | Maximum recipients accepted for one message. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `limits.auth.failures_per_net` | int | `5` | system | Failed authentication attempts allowed per client network (grouped by network.ipv4_prefix and network.ipv6_prefix) within limits.auth.window. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `limits.auth.failures_per_user` | int | `10` | system | Failed authentication attempts allowed per user name within limits.auth.window. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `limits.auth.window` | duration | `"15m"` | system | Time window in which failed authentication attempts are counted; a duration such as 90, 30s, 15m, 1h or 7d (a bare number is seconds). Allowed: at least 1. |
| `limits.user.messages_per_minute` | int | `30` | sender | Maximum messages one authenticated user may send per minute. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `limits.user.messages_per_hour` | int | `300` | sender | Maximum messages one authenticated user may send per hour. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `limits.user.recipients_per_hour` | int | `1000` | sender | Maximum recipients one authenticated user may address per hour. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `penalty_box.threshold` | int | `50` | system | IP score at which a client network is put into the penalty box. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `penalty_box.score_cap` | int | `100` | system | Highest score an IP can accumulate. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `penalty_box.score_ttl` | duration | `"24h"` | system | Time after which an IP score decays to zero without new offences; a duration such as 30m, 24h or 7d (a bare number is seconds). Allowed: at least 1. |
| `penalty_box.ladder` | list[duration] | `["24h", "7d", "30d"]` | system | Ban durations for the first, second and later offences of the same client; a list of durations such as ["24h", "7d", "30d"] (a bare number is seconds). The last one repeats for further offences. Allowed: at least 1; not empty. |
| `penalty_box.history` | duration | `"90d"` | system | How long past offences are remembered when choosing the next ban duration; a duration such as 30d or 90d (a bare number is seconds). Allowed: at least 1. |
| `abuse.protocol_error_ip_score` | int | `10` | system | Score added to the client IP when a session exceeds its protocol error limit; 0 adds nothing. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `abuse.invalid_recipient_ip_score` | int | `10` | system | Score added to the client IP when a session exceeds its invalid recipient limit; 0 adds nothing. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `abuse.relay_denied_ip_score` | int | `10` | system | Score added to the client IP for an attempt to relay to a non-local domain; 0 adds nothing. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `abuse.auth_failure_ip_score` | int | `10` | system | Score added to the client IP when it tries to authenticate again after a temporary authentication failure; 0 adds nothing. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `checks.conn_limits.mode` | str | `"block"` | system | Mode of the connection limits check: off disables it, block rejects when it fails, monitor only logs, score adds msg_score to the message score, test logs what block would do. ip_score applies in every mode except off. Allowed: one of off, block, monitor, score, test. |
| `checks.conn_limits.ip_score` | int | `5` | system | Penalty-box score added to the client IP when the connection limits check fails, in every mode except off; 0 adds nothing. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `checks.conn_limits.msg_score` | int | `0` | system | Score added to the message when the connection limits check fails; used only in score mode, where 0 adds nothing. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `checks.conn_limits.timeout_ms` | int | `1000` | system | Maximum time in milliseconds the connection limits check may take before it is skipped. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `checks.penalty_box.mode` | str | `"block"` | system | Mode of the penalty box check: off disables it, block rejects when it fails, monitor only logs, score adds msg_score to the message score, test logs what block would do. ip_score applies in every mode except off. Allowed: one of off, block, monitor, score, test. |
| `checks.penalty_box.ip_score` | int | `0` | system | Penalty-box score added to the client IP when the penalty box check fails, in every mode except off; 0 adds nothing. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `checks.penalty_box.msg_score` | int | `0` | system | Score added to the message when the penalty box check fails; used only in score mode, where 0 adds nothing. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `checks.penalty_box.timeout_ms` | int | `1000` | system | Maximum time in milliseconds the penalty box check may take before it is skipped. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `checks.session_limits.mode` | str | `"block"` | system | Mode of the session limits check: off disables it, block rejects when it fails, monitor only logs, score adds msg_score to the message score, test logs what block would do. ip_score applies in every mode except off. Allowed: one of off, block, monitor, score, test. |
| `checks.session_limits.ip_score` | int | `0` | system | Penalty-box score added to the client IP when the session limits check fails, in every mode except off; 0 adds nothing. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `checks.session_limits.msg_score` | int | `0` | system | Score added to the message when the session limits check fails; used only in score mode, where 0 adds nothing. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `checks.session_limits.timeout_ms` | int | `1000` | system | Maximum time in milliseconds the session limits check may take before it is skipped. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `checks.auth_limits.mode` | str | `"block"` | system | Mode of the authentication limits check: off disables it, block rejects when it fails, monitor only logs, score adds msg_score to the message score, test logs what block would do. ip_score applies in every mode except off. Allowed: one of off, block, monitor, score, test. |
| `checks.auth_limits.ip_score` | int | `20` | system | Penalty-box score added to the client IP when the authentication limits check fails, in every mode except off; 0 adds nothing. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `checks.auth_limits.msg_score` | int | `0` | system | Score added to the message when the authentication limits check fails; used only in score mode, where 0 adds nothing. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `checks.auth_limits.timeout_ms` | int | `1000` | system | Maximum time in milliseconds the authentication limits check may take before it is skipped. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `checks.user_rate.mode` | str | `"block"` | sender | Mode of the per-user rate limit check: off disables it, block rejects when it fails, monitor only logs, score adds msg_score to the message score, test logs what block would do. ip_score applies in every mode except off. Allowed: one of off, block, monitor, score, test. |
| `checks.user_rate.ip_score` | int | `0` | sender | Penalty-box score added to the client IP when the per-user rate limit check fails, in every mode except off; 0 adds nothing. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `checks.user_rate.msg_score` | int | `0` | sender | Score added to the message when the per-user rate limit check fails; used only in score mode, where 0 adds nothing. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `checks.user_rate.timeout_ms` | int | `1000` | sender | Maximum time in milliseconds the per-user rate limit check may take before it is skipped. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `testmode` | bool | `false` | recipient | When true, messages are only tagged and logged and never rejected. |
| `scoring.limit` | int | `50` | recipient | Message score at or above which the message is rejected. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `scoring.warn` | int | `35` | recipient | Message score at or above which the message is marked as suspicious. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `scoring.add_header` | bool | `true` | recipient | Add an X-ASSP-NG header with the score and reasons to accepted messages. |
| `scoring.warn_subject_tag` | str | `""` | recipient | Text prepended to the subject of suspicious messages; empty disables tagging. |
| `timeouts.tls_handshake` | int | `30` | system | Seconds allowed for a TLS handshake. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `timeouts.backend_connect` | int | `10` | system | Seconds allowed to connect to the backend mail server. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `timeouts.backend_banner` | int | `30` | system | Seconds to wait for the backend greeting banner. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `timeouts.command` | int | `300` | system | Seconds a client may be idle between SMTP commands. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `timeouts.data_block` | int | `180` | system | Seconds allowed between data blocks while a message is received. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `timeouts.data_total` | int | `600` | system | Seconds allowed to receive one complete message. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `timeouts.backend_command` | int | `300` | system | Seconds to wait for the backend to answer an SMTP command. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `timeouts.backend_final` | int | `600` | system | Seconds to wait for the backend answer after the end of message data. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `timeouts.shutdown` | int | `30` | system | Seconds that open sessions get to finish when the service stops. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `timeouts.ptr` | int | `3` | system | Seconds allowed for the reverse DNS lookup of the client address. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `buffer.memory_per_message` | int | `1048576` | system | Bytes of one message kept in memory before it spills to the spool directory. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `buffer.memory_total` | int | `134217728` | system | Total bytes of message data kept in memory across all sessions. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `max_message_size` | int | `52428800` | system | Maximum accepted message size in bytes. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `paths.spool` | str | `"/var/lib/assp-ng/spool"` | system | Directory for spooled message data. |
| `paths.cache` | str | `"/var/lib/assp-ng/cache"` | system | Directory for cached data. |
| `paths.run` | str | `"/run/assp-ng"` | system | Directory for runtime files such as sockets. |
| `paths.log_dir` | str | `"/var/log/assp-ng"` | system | Directory for log files. |
| `health.listen` | str | `"127.0.0.1:8025"` | system | Address and port of the health check endpoint, as host:port. |
| `alerts.email` | str | `""` | system | Email address that receives alerts; empty disables email alerts. |
| `alerts.webhook` | str | `""` | system | Webhook URL that receives alerts; empty disables the webhook. |
| `alerts.smtp_server` | str | `"127.0.0.1:10125"` | system | SMTP server, as host:port, used to deliver alert email. |
| `alerts.min_interval` | duration | `"30m"` | system | Minimum time between two alerts about the same problem; a duration such as 30m or 1h (a bare number is seconds). Allowed: at least 1. |
| `log.level` | str | `"info"` | system | Minimum severity written to the log. Allowed: one of debug, info, warning, error. |
| `debug.max_size_mb` | int | `100` | system | Maximum total size of debug logs in megabytes. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `debug.default_duration` | duration | `"30m"` | system | How long a debug session lasts when no duration is given; a duration such as 30m or 2h (a bare number is seconds). Allowed: at least 1. |
| `debug.max_duration` | duration | `"24h"` | system | Longest allowed debug session for a single client or user; a duration such as 24h (a bare number is seconds). Allowed: at least 1. |
| `debug.max_duration_all` | duration | `"1h"` | system | Longest allowed debug session covering all traffic; a duration such as 1h (a bare number is seconds). Allowed: at least 1. |
| `debug.ring_lines` | int | `50` | system | Number of recent log lines kept per session for debug output; 0 keeps none. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `memory.soft_limit_mb` | int | `360` | system | Process memory in megabytes above which caches are trimmed. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `memory.idle_trim_after_s` | int | `60` | system | Seconds without open sessions after which freed memory is returned to the system; 0 trims as soon as the instance is idle. Allowed: at least 0. |
| `memory.trim_interval_s` | int | `600` | system | Seconds between periodic memory trims. Allowed: at least 1. |
| `domains.refresh_interval_s` | int | `300` | system | Seconds between reloads of the list of local domains. Allowed: at least 1. |
